setting.casual_explanation: A same-named `AllowRemoteDASD` value appears under Session Manager I/O on the clean baseline, but the live current-build evidence points to the removable-storage policy family instead.

setting.tradeoffs_overview: The current-build evidence stack now converges on a collision story rather than an active Session Manager I/O tweak. The old baseline value exists, but the strongest static, live-kernel, and first-party policy evidence all point to the removable-storage policy key instead.
setting.professional_notes: Phase-0 existence confirmed AllowRemoteDASD on the live Win25H2Clean baseline with preview value 0 under Session Manager I/O System. The path-aware static pass over the narrowed binary set found an exact current-build ntoskrnl.exe value hit for AllowRemoteDASD, but no exact intended path-context string in the narrowed exact-string scan. The decisive current-build Ghidra export then showed the naturally resolved ntoskrnl.exe function opening \REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices and querying AllowRemoteDASD there. A tools-hardened path-aware ETW lane then ran both short and split I/O-burst traces against the intended Session Manager I/O path on RegProbe-Baseline-ToolsHardened-20260330. It produced real ETL/CSV outputs, kept shell health clean, and still returned a clean no-hit for both the exact value name and the intended path. A Linux KVM Procmon replay then ran a raw I/O burst, produced a real 267176-line CSV, and still returned zero lines containing the intended Session Manager I/O path, AllowRemoteDASD itself, or the removable-storage collision path. A debugger-assisted KVM local-KD follow-up then attached to the live guest kernel, resolved `nt!IopAllowRemoteDASD` directly, and returned the current-build symbol address without timing out. A deeper local-KD disassembly and string-dump follow-up on the same guest then showed `IopAllowRemoteDASD` calling `IopOpenRegistryKey` and `IopGetRegistryValue`, with its live path literal resolving to `\REGISTRY\MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices` and its live value-name literal resolving to `AllowRemoteDASD`. Microsoft Learn now documents that same value name as the removable-storage policy setting `All Removable Storage: Allow direct access in remote sessions`, mapped to `Software\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\RemovableStorageDevices`. Taken together, the active current-build route is no longer meaningfully ambiguous: the historical Session Manager I/O value remains an observed baseline artifact, but the live control surface resolves to the removable-storage policy family instead.
